key_insight: RoboJEPA is a scalable latent world model for robotics that learns to predict and plan in compact representations rather than raw observations. The paper shows how model size, data, and compute affect robotic imagination, helping turn world-model scaling into something measurable and actionable.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the lack of a principled way to evaluate how robotic latent world models improve as they grow with more parameters, more data, and more compute. This makes it hard to know how to build stronger planning and prediction models for real-world robots.
method: Trains a JEPA-based latent world model called RoboJEPA on a large-scale dataset covering 12 different robotic embodiments.
Learns predictive representations of future states for planning and imagination in latent space instead of pixel-level forecasting.
Studies scaling behavior to understand how performance changes with model size, dataset scale, and compute budget.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this provides a practical framework for building and scaling robot world models more systematically. It can guide model design and training decisions for more capable robotic prediction, planning, and generalization across embodiments.

paper_title: RoboJEPA: Scaling Robotic Latent World Models
paper_authors: Artem Zholus, Nicolas Beltran-Velez, Jianhao Yuan, Sarath Chandar, Tushar Nagarajan
